results.title: Cost Allocation Methods – ACCOUNTING 4 REAL
results.content: # Cost Allocation Methods. A number of methods used for cost allocation:. In the single-rate cost allocation method fixed and variable costs are considered as ONE POOL. A single cost allocation rate per unit is used for both variable costs and fixed costs. Dual rate cost allocation method categorizes cost into TWO types of cost pools: fixed costs and variable costs. Variable cost pool and fixed cost pool each have their own appropriate cost allocation rate. For both the single-rate method and the dual-rate methods costs can be allocated basing either on a budgeted rate or actual cost rate. **Budgeted cost rate is PREFERRED** for cost allocation. Actual cost rate is not recommended and not widely used in practice. **Single-rate method vs dual-rate method**. Advantage of the single-rate method is low implementation costs. Single-rate method doesn’t require  detailed analysis to classify the costs into fixed and variable pools. Disadvantage of the single-rate method is that it could lead to managerial decisions favorable for one department, but not efficient for organization as a whole. Advantage of the dual-rate method is that it takes into account behavioral difference of fixed costs and variable costs. Information provided by the dual-rate method  favorable for organization as a whole and each division. Disadvantage of the dual-rate method is cost associated with its implementation. **Methods to allocate support costs to operating departments:**. Direct cost allocation method ignores ant services provided by one support division to another support division. Step-down cost allocation method recognizes the cost of services provided by one support division to another support division prior to allocating cost pool for remaining services to the core divisions. Reciprocal cost allocation method aimed to adjust budgeted costs to include in divisions’ cost pools cost of mutual services provided by support departments. **Methods for common costs allocation (***i.e. costs share by two or more divisions***):**. Under stand-alone cost allocation method information related to each cost object used to determine the cost allocation rate. Under incremental cost allocation method individual cost objects are ranked and costs are allocated between cost objects using this ranking. + ACCOUNTING 4 REAL* Already have a WordPress.com account?
